v00.transcript: Welcome to O Lake Foods. This guide shows you how to open an account and place your first order.

v01.transcript: To open a wholesale account, choose Become a Customer on the O-Lake Foods website.

v02.transcript: Fill in your business name, your contact details, and your delivery address.

v03.transcript: Add a short note about your kitchen, then send the application.

v04.transcript: The O-Lake team reviews your application.

v05.transcript: Once you're approved, sign in with your email and password.

v06.transcript: Your portal opens on the dashboard with your catalog, your offers, and your orders.

v07.transcript: Your catalog shows a photo of every product with the price set for your account.

v08.transcript: supply team. Search by name or filter by category to find an item quickly.

v09.transcript: Tap Add. To put an item in your cart, add as many as you need.

v10.transcript: Open the cart to check the quantities, then choose Checkout.

v11.transcript: Choose delivery or pickup and add a note for the team if you need to.

v12.transcript: Submit the order. Payment stays on your usual account terms.

v13.transcript: your order is received. The team confirms it next.

v14.transcript: Under My Orders, each order shows its status. Received. Confirmed. Ready. Then completed.

v15.transcript: Open an order to see its items, its total, and your note.

v16.transcript: Every order has an invoice, print it or save it as a PDF.

v17.transcript: Your statement lists the products and the orders for any period you choose.

v18.transcript: Offers shows the promotions your O-Lake rep has set up for you.

v19.transcript: Account holds your contacts, your delivery address, and your payment terms.

v20.transcript: That's everything you need to place and follow your orders.

a00.transcript: Welcome! This guide walks you through the O Lake Foods Admin, one task at a time.

a01.transcript: Sign in to the admin with your email. Only the emails on the admin list have access.

a02.transcript: The dashboard is your starting point. New orders show first.

a03.transcript: Choose orders in the sidebar to see every order.

a04.transcript: The new tab lists the orders waiting for you. Open one to see it in full.

a05.transcript: Check the items, the profit on each line, and the customer's note.

a06.transcript: Choose Confirm. The stock is deducted and the order shows as confirmed.

a07.transcript: When it's packed, mark it prepared. Then mark it complete.

a09.transcript: It carries your business details, the customer's details and every line. Print it or save it as a PDF.

a10.transcript: new applications arrive in leads. Review 1, then set its status to approved.

a11.transcript: To add the customer, pick the approved lead and convert it.

a12.transcript: The new customer joins your list with their status and payment terms.

a13.transcript: Open the customer to invite them to the portal. Send email delivers the invite.

a14.transcript: No email? Copy the invite link and share it yourself.

a15.transcript: Catalog visibility controls which products this customer can see.

a16.transcript: Each customer has their own price on every product assigned to them.

a17.transcript: Products lists the stock, the cost, and the sale price of every item.

a18.transcript: Choose Add Product, then enter the code, the name and the pack size.

a19.transcript: Enter the cost and the price. Your cost stays private. Customers only see the price.

a20.transcript: create the product. It appears in the list ready to assign.

a22.transcript: Assign products chooses which customers can order each item.

a23.transcript: Pricing sets a default margin for the whole catalog.

a24.transcript: A margin for a product, a category, or a customer overrides the default.

a25.transcript: Analytics shows your revenue over the period you choose.

a26.transcript: Below the chart, each product's units, revenue, and profit.

a27.transcript: Reports builds a printable summary. Pick a preset or tick the sections you need.

a28.transcript: Every document prints with your business details at the top.

a29.transcript: A customer statement lists their products and orders for the period you pick.

a30.transcript: The product list shows the whole catalog, with stock and prices.

a31.transcript: low stock lists the items to reorder, each with what's left.

a32.transcript: Unavailable products lists anything customers can't order right now.

a33.transcript: button. That's the admin tour. Every document has a print button when you need paper.

f00.transcript: This film follows one restaurant through the whole O'Lake system, from its first visit to its invoices.

f01.transcript: On the left is what a visitor or customer sees on a phone. On the right is the O Lake Admin on a desktop.

f02.transcript: When something on one side causes a change on the other, a line of light links the two. The categories on the public site come straight from the admins category list.

f03.transcript: Each category page lists the products the admin keeps active with their photos. Prices stay private until a customer signs in.

f04.transcript: A restaurant owner wants to buy from O Lake. On the home page, they tap Become a Customer.

f05.transcript: They fill in the application, business name, contact, email, phone, and address.

f06.transcript: They add the type of business and a short note and submit. Now watch the admin side. The application appears on the leads page, marked New.

f07.transcript: The phone confirms that the application was received. The dashboard also lists it under recent leads.

f08.transcript: The site also has a contact form and a supplier form. Those messages are saved, but the admin does not show them yet.

f09.transcript: On the leads page, the admin reviews the application and marks it approved.

f10.transcript: Approved leads wait on the Add a Customer page. One click converts the lead into a customer account.

f11.transcript: The new account opens with a setup checklist. It is not invited yet and it has no products.

f12.transcript: The admin can send an invitation by email or copy a one-time link to send by message. The customer opens it and sees a welcome page with their business name.

f13.transcript: They choose a password and save it. They are now signed in to their own portal and on the admin side the account shows as active.

f14.transcript: Their catalog is still empty. Nothing is visible until the admin sets it up.

f15.transcript: The admin opens Add Product and picks the items this restaurant buys.

f16.transcript: As soon as they are added, the customer's catalog fills up. Each product shows a price marked your price.

f17.transcript: Each price comes from the margin rules. The table shows the cost, the list price, the customer's price, the profit, and the rule behind it.

f18.transcript: The admin can also type a price by hand. The customer sees the new price in their catalog.

f19.transcript: A margin for this customer reprises every product that follows the rules. Prices typed by hand stay as they are.

f20.transcript: Catalog visibility can open whole categories. The extra products show at the list price without the your price label.

f21.transcript: A hidden product disappears from this customer's catalog even when it is assigned.

f22.transcript: Assign products does the same for many customers at once, with a preview of cost and profit before anything changes.

f23.transcript: The margin rules page holds the global, product, category and customer margins. A new rule updates the affected customer prices automatically.

f24.transcript: From the customer page, the admin can also recompute prices, change many prices at once, copy a catalog from another customer, or export it.

f25.transcript: Offers are set per customer. Here the admin creates a welcome offer on salmon for two weeks.

f26.transcript: The offer appears right away on the customer's offers page

f27.transcript: In the catalog, the salmon now shows the offer price, with the regular price struck through.

f28.transcript: An offer template can be applied to many customers in one step. The preview shows exactly what will change and the customer sees the new offer.

f29.transcript: Running now lists the active offers and each applied batch which can be undone as a whole.

f30.transcript: The customer searches the catalog and adds salmon to the cart.

f31.transcript: They add cream, takeout cups, and oat milk, choosing the quantities as they go.

f32.transcript: The cart shows the exact price of each line, including the offer.

f33.transcript: At checkout they choose delivery or pickup and can leave a note. There is no online payment. The order follows the account's payment terms.

f34.transcript: They submit the order. Now watch the admin side. It appears at once in the new tab, with a number in the sidebar and an alert sound.

f35.transcript: on the phone the order shows as received the dashboard counts it as waiting for confirmation

f36.transcript: The admin opens the order. Each line shows its cost and profit, which the customer never sees.

f37.transcript: When the admin confirms, the system checks the stock. There are not enough takeout cups.

f38.transcript: The admin confirms anyway. The stock is taken out, and on the customer's phone, the order is now confirmed.

f39.transcript: The cups are now unavailable to every customer. The Oat Milk came from an open category, so it is now part of this customer's catalog.

f40.transcript: When the order is packed the admin marks it prepared the customer sees ready

f41.transcript: Once it is handed over, the admin completes it and the customer sees completed.

f42.transcript: A second order can be cancelled with a reason that stays with the admin. The customer sees cancelled and any stock taken for it goes back.

f43.transcript: Both sides keep the full order history and the admin lists can be filtered by date.

f44.transcript: Each order has an invoice. Both sides print the same document with the business details at the top.

f45.transcript: The customer's statement for a period matches the admin's customer copy.

f46.transcript: The admin also has an internal copy, with cost and profit, clearly marked as internal.

f47.transcript: A cancelled order keeps its invoice marked as cancelled for the record.

f48.transcript: Back on the admin side confirming the order reduced the stock. The cups now show as oversold.

f49.transcript: The dashboard shows today's revenue and profit and flags the low stock.

f50.transcript: The low stock and unavailable statements list what needs reordering.

f51.transcript: When new stock arrives, the admin receives it. It settles the oversold units first, and the cups are available again for customers.

f52.transcript: Analytics shows the revenue trend, best sellers, top customers, and customers who have gone quiet.

f53.transcript: The report builder prints a summary for any period. Adding cost and profit turns it into an internal report.

f54.transcript: The product list can be printed for customers or with cost columns for internal use.

f55.transcript: The Admin adds a new product with its photo, cost, price, and starting stock.

f56.transcript: Once it is created, it appears on the public site, still without a price.

f57.transcript: When a product is set to inactive, it leaves the public site.

f58.transcript: It also leaves every customer's catalog.

f59.transcript: Categories can have one level of subcategories, which customers see in their catalog filter.

f60.transcript: When the admin edits the account, the customer's account page shows the new details.

f61.transcript: If the account is suspended, the customer can no longer open the portal.

f62.transcript: Setting it back to active restores access with the catalog and prices kept.

f63.transcript: Customers can reset their own password from the sign-in page. Admins use a separate sign-in, open only to approved emails.

f64.transcript: Finally, order alerts can be switched on, so a sound plays when a new order arrives.

f65.transcript: That is the full loop from application to invoice on both sides of O Lake.

f02b.transcript: The public catalog page shows the same categories, each with its own page of products.

f07b.transcript: On the Leads page, tabs sort the applications by status, new, contacted, approved, and rejected.

f10b.transcript: An account can also be created by hand, under manual entry, for a customer who did not apply online.

f13b.transcript: The welcome banner appears only on this first visit to the portal.

f29b.transcript: Templates are reusable offers, such as a weekend promotion, kept in the offer library.

f36b.transcript: The order also shows who placed it, with the note left at checkout.

f41b.transcript: The customer's order page always shows the current status and refreshes on its own.

f45b.transcript: A statement can be printed for any period using the period filter at the top.

f48b.transcript: The dashboard also lists today's top products and top customers, with links to the full analytics.

f49b.transcript: The dashboard also flags customers who were invited, but have not signed in yet, so the team can follow up.

f50b.transcript: On the products page, low and oversold stock is flagged in the stock column.

f52b.transcript: Further down, Analytics shows the best sellers by units, revenue and profit and the products that are not moving.

f08b.transcript: The site also has pages about the company, delivery, and common questions.

f62b.transcript: The customer list shows every account with its status, phone, payment terms, and catalog size.
